# atlassian_jira_permission_grant (Resource)

Attach a permission grant to a Jira permission scheme. Grants define who (group or project role) has which permission (e.g. BROWSE_PROJECTS).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Grant BROWSE_PROJECTS to a group within a permission scheme.
# Replace scheme_id with an existing permission scheme ID and set group_id or group_name.
resource "atlassian_jira_permission_grant" "browse_group" {
  scheme_id   = "10000"
  permission  = "BROWSE_PROJECTS"
  holder_type = "group"
  group_name  = "jira-users"
  # Or use group_id for stability: group_id = "abc-123-def"
}

output "grant_id" {
  value = atlassian_jira_permission_grant.browse_group.id
}
```

## Import

Import by scheme ID and grant ID in the form `scheme_id/grant_id`. The resource block must exist in config before importing.

```bash
terraform import atlassian_jira_permission_grant.grant 10000/10001
```

**Import ID:** `scheme_id/grant_id` (e.g. `10000/10001`). See [Importing resources](../import.md) for more.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `holder_type` (String) Type of holder: `group` or `projectRole`.
- `permission` (String) Permission key (e.g. BROWSE_PROJECTS, ADMINISTER_PROJECTS, VIEW_DEVICE_TOOLS).
- `scheme_id` (String) ID of the permission scheme.

### Optional

- `group_id` (String) Group ID (when holder_type is group). Prefer this over group_name for stability.
- `group_name` (String) Group name (when holder_type is group). Use group_id when possible.
- `project_role_id` (String) Project role ID (when holder_type is projectRole).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite ID: scheme_id/grant_id (set after create).
